lesson.title: Review Day: America and the Roaring Twenties
lesson.subject: social-studies

contentBlocks.text: This week you traced America from the war through a decade of real change. Let's review it all!

Quick review: the US entered WWI in 1917, driven partly by submarine attacks (Day 1). The US emerged from the war with greater global influence (Day 2). The 1920s brought real cultural change, including new social norms for women (Day 3). The decade also brought a genuine economic boom fueled partly by buying on credit (Day 4). Write a short paragraph explaining how these four events connect to form one coherent story of America's transformation in this era.
Great work this week — you traced America's transformation from WWI through the Roaring Twenties! Next week we'll continue this story.

objectives: Review US entry into WWI, its aftermath, 1920s cultural change, and the economic boom
Write a short paragraph connecting all four events into one coherent transformation narrative
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child write their connecting paragraph.
3. Complete the review worksheet.
4. Celebrate finishing a full week of early 20th-century US history!
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just two of the four events the child remembers best rather than requiring all four in the paragraph
Ready for more: ask the child to predict what economic risk a boom built partly on credit-based borrowing might eventually create
This is a good checkpoint to note which of the week's four events needs the most reinforcement going forward
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended synthesis activity — check that the paragraph connects at least two or three of the week's events into a coherent narrative of a nation entering a major war, emerging with new global influence, and experiencing real cultural and economic transformation at home in the years that followed.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's WA Social Studies and C3 Framework History/Economics/Culture standards before the course continues, matching the established Day-5-review pacing used across every unit this session.
